body:
Resolved so far: the key-soundness reviews and repairs in PR #638 (`0659da2be`), #646 (`2e9362a69`), #649 (`2bbadf8f0`), #651 (`3ac5e41b8`), and #653 (`ef4570f32`) are merged. Niger's wider EXTENSION repair subsequently landed as `d0ec4b32f` (#679, now closed). Core's most-complete-observed-row policy landed in `c55fc6012` (#871, closed). This reconciliation reads source at `ab41e389ea010195b647f4e5345f914c707e57c2`; it does not repeat those historical data builds.

## Corrected scope

The original **49 sites** were a historical inventory, not 49 confirmed corruption defects. The proposal to blanket-replace `.first()` with `.first(skipna=False)` was withdrawn in the [correction thread](https://github.com/ligon/LSMS_Library/issues/637#issuecomment-5038336539). Later #871 establishes the current core row-selection policy; it is not authorization to replace every country-specific reducer mechanically.

This issue remains open for **key-soundness review of the original lower-risk first/last aggregation tail**, reconciling later changes before proposing any fix. A duplicate-free table can still use the wrong identifier namespace; exact/complementary payloads alone do not prove two records describe the same entity. Fix a broken identifier or missing grain at its source rather than hiding it with a reducer.

## Completed review blocks

| Block | Disposition / evidence |
|---|---|
| Six EHCVM people_last7days sites | Source key/merge reviews completed; #638. |
| Six other sites: Burkina Faso, EthiopiaRHS, Uganda, Niger | Reviewed in #646; Uganda plot_inputs gained season there, Uganda crop condition followed in #649, Niger household EXTENSION followed under #679. |
| Tanzania's 21 listed sites | Reviewed in #651; the UPHI/household-key repair and documented no-op/de-replication cases landed. Its community-price choice remains separately tracked by #840. |
| Malawi's three direct multi-column `.first()` sites | Reviewed and guarded by #653 / `tests/test_gh637_malawi_first_sites.py`. |
| Core collapses | #871 now selects an observed row and preserves separate additive/provenance behavior. Do not redo the old proposed core replacement. |

## Remaining audit inventory

The original tail contained 11 sites. A static scan finds these current counterparts; **pending reconciliation is not a claim that all 11 are defective or have never received later tests**. Read later changes, including sale-basis and derivation work, before measuring.

| Module | Current callable / aggregation to reconcile |
|---|---|
| `Malawi/_/malawi.py` | `_consolidate_harvest` — first-selected crop/planting/harvest attributes |
| same | `assemble_crop_production` — first-selected sale/branch/harvest attributes |
| same | `assemble_plot_inputs` — purchased/improved attributes |
| same | `assemble_livestock` — ValuePerAnimal |
| same | `assemble_anthropometry` — Weight/Height/Age_months/Sex |
| same | `assemble_plot_labor` — Wage |
| same | `assemble_people_last7days` — person work variables |
| same | `assemble_community_prices` — Price/NumberOfUnits/Available |
| `Nigeria/_/nigeria.py` | `community_prices_for_wave` — now Price and Derivation (the original entry was single-column) |
| `Tanzania/_/tanzania.py` | `crop_production_for_wave` — unit and sale fields alongside quantity sums |
| same | `plot_inputs_for_wave` — unit alongside quantity sums |

## Completion criteria

1. Map each original tail entry to current source and any existing measured review/test; mark superseded or already-verified entries explicitly. Report new/split sites separately rather than silently treating the old 49 as a current census.
2. For genuinely unreviewed sites, read country CONTENTS first and establish the source grain and identifier namespace per wave. Measure merge fan-out, null-key handling, distinct source entities and conflicting observed values. Aggregate overlap or a zero duplicate count alone is insufficient.
3. Observe the actual script path: an in-process GroupBy monkeypatch does not see a `make` subprocess. The early zero-result probe in this thread was invalidated; later reviews used direct source measurement or `runpy` with isolated data roots.
4. Repair only demonstrated key/grain defects; preserve accepted survey-specific transformations. Add meaningful regression guards for measured invariants. Where a genuine semantic choice remains, state it with evidence and link a specific owner (e.g. #840), instead of counting it as reviewed and resolved.
5. Replace this inventory with the final per-site dispositions before closing. An explicit-skipna lint, if desired, is a separate readability proposal and not a correctness fix.

Current contracts: `SkunkWorks/grain_aggregation_policy.org`, `most_complete_row`, and the existing grain/reducer tests. Historical review records and this issue's correction comments remain evidence, but older completion doctrine must not override the subsequently adopted #871 core policy.

Tier: diagnose first; no blanket reducer rewrite is authorized by this issue.

comments.body:
## Correction to the premise — the composite is usually CORRECT

I filed this arguing that `.first()`'s per-column NA-skipping fabricates rows, and proposed `.first(skipna=False)` as the fix. **That was wrong, and the proposed fix is a regression.** Recording it here because the reasoning is attractive and someone will re-derive it.

`NaN` is **absence, not contradiction** in this codebase. If one row records `Region` and another records `Rural`, the group has both, and combining them discards no observed value. The repo's own `reduce_to_agreed` returns the *same composite deliberately* — see `test_nan_is_absence_not_contradiction` in `tests/test_gh323_explicit_reducers.py`.

Verified on pandas 3.0.2:

| | Region | Rural |
|---|---|---|
| input row 1 | Dakar | `<NA>` |
| input row 2 | `NaN` | True |
| `reduce_to_agreed` | Dakar | **True** |
| `.first(skipna=True)` | Dakar | **True** |
| `.first(skipna=False)` | Dakar | **`<NA>`** ← drops an observed value |

So `skipna=False` would return `<NA>` for values the survey actually recorded. A PR for it was drafted and **abandoned on this evidence**.

## What survives

**The composite is wrong only when the rows describe DIFFERENT REAL ENTITIES** — two clusters merged by a key that is unique only within a district, or two people collapsed onto one `pid`. That is a **broken identifier**, and GH #323 D1 says fix the identifier. No reducer can detect it, because both readings are consistent with the data.

So this issue is best read as **an inventory of sites whose correctness depends on their key being sound**, not as a list of bugs. The 49 sites are where a broken key would silently produce a merged entity instead of an error.

Note the codebase already contains both readings, in tension: `country._collapse_to_cluster_grain`'s docstring condemns the composite ("it yields a COMPOSITE ... exists nowhere in the survey") while `reduce_to_agreed`, its sanctioned replacement, produces the identical composite on purpose. Both cannot be right; the distinction above is what reconciles them.

## Revised remediation

1. ~~`.first(skipna=False)` in core~~ — **withdrawn**, it is a regression.
2. The real defect at #323 Site 1/2 is the *arbitrary resolution of genuine disagreement* (two distinct **observed** values), which `.first()` does while warning. That is the Option-B discussion, not this issue.
3. The site inventory below stays useful for key-soundness review — the EHCVM `people_last7days` cluster especially, where a merged entity is a person who was never enumerated.
4. A lint preferring an explicit `skipna=` is still worth having, now for *readability* rather than correctness: `.first()` reading as `first_row()` is exactly the misreading that produced this issue.

## Runtime probe

Countries built cold, counting output value-combinations absent from the input (a lower bound):

| country | tables | `first()` sites | combos absent from input |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Benin | 21 | 1 | 0 |
| Guinea-Bissau | 21 | 1 | 0 |
| Togo | 21 | 1 | 0 |
| EthiopiaRHS | 17 | 0 | 0 |

Consistent with the corrected reading: the EHCVM duplicates are exact, not complementary, so no completion even occurs.

PR #636 has been amended — the `xfail` that claimed a live defect is removed, and a test now pins the completion doctrine so this regression cannot be introduced later.

## Probe results — and a methodological failure that invalidates my earlier read

**Correction first.** In my previous comment I reported "Benin 0, Guinea-Bissau 0, Togo 0" and inferred *"the EHCVM duplicates are exact, not complementary, so no completion even occurs."* **That inference was unfounded.** The probe never observed those sites at all.

The probe monkeypatches `DataFrameGroupBy.first` **in-process**. But `people_last7days` is declared `materialize: make` in Benin, Niger and the other EHCVM countries — script-path tables run **out-of-process**, via `subprocess.run(make_cmd, ...)` (`country.py:1115`). The patch does not exist in those subprocesses.

So **all 38 country-script sites are UNMEASURED.** Every site the probe actually caught is in core:

| country | tables | site | calls | rows in→out | combos absent from input |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| Uganda | 27 | `country.py:4680` (Site 1) | 10 | 112,312→83,327 | **21** |
| Niger | 22 | `country.py:4680` | 16 | 346,321→326,864 | **13** |
| Burkina Faso | 23 | `country.py:4680` | 4 | 234,933→218,378 | **5** |
| CotedIvoire | 21 | `country.py:4680` | 8 | 49,504→31,594 | 0 |
| Senegal | 21 | `country.py:4680` | 3 | 24,192→11,095 | 0 |
| Guinea-Bissau | 21 | `country.py:4680` | 2 | 17,598→11,029 | 0 |
| Benin / Togo | 21 | `country.py:4680` | 1 | 8,012→670 / 6,171→540 | 0 |
| Burkina Faso / Niger / Uganda | — | `country.py:4536` (Site 2) | 1–2 | — | 0 |

**Total: 39 rows** whose value-combination did not appear in the input, all at **Site 1**, none at Site 2.

## What the 39 mean

Under the corrected reading in the comment above, these are **completions**, not defects — a group whose rows carry complementary missingness, combined into a fuller record that discards no observed value. They are correct *provided the key is sound*. Where they would be wrong is if the key merges two distinct entities, and the probe cannot distinguish those cases; only key review can.

So: no defect demonstrated, and none excluded either.

## To actually measure the country-script sites

The patch has to reach the subprocess. A `sitecustomize.py` on the child `PYTHONPATH` that installs the same wrapper and writes a per-process JSON would do it — `run_make_target` already threads a custom `env`, so the hook can ride along. That is the missing half of this audit and is not done.

Until then, the 38 country-script sites in the inventory below have **not** been exercised, and any claim about them — including mine — is unsupported.

## EHCVM `people_last7days` cluster (6 sites) — reviewed. **No key is broken.**

Closing out the six copy-pasted EHCVM sites from the inventory. Per the correction thread, these are not bugs to fix but **sites whose correctness depends on their key being sound**, so the deliverable is a key review, not a patch. PR #638 lands the evidence only — a comment at each site — with no behaviour change.

**Result: the collapse is a strict no-op in all six countries.** Not "the composites it forms are benign" — it forms none. There are zero duplicate `(t, i, pid)` groups anywhere.

### Method (and why the earlier number was meaningless)

Measured on the **source** with `get_dataframe()`, not by instrumenting the build. As you noted, these tables are `materialize: make` and run out-of-process, so the in-process `DataFrameGroupBy.first` monkeypatch never saw them — the reported `0` for Benin / Guinea-Bissau / Togo was an artefact of the probe's blind spot, not a measurement. This replaces it with a real one.

For each country: load `s04_me_*` + `s01_me_*`, reproduce the merge and the `i()`/`pid` construction exactly as the site does, count duplicate groups on the built key, classify each as exact / complementary / conflicting.

### Per-country

| country | s04 rows | s01 rows | dup groups on `(grappe, menage, s01q00a)` s04 / s01 | merge fan-out | groups on `(t,i,pid)` | **dup groups** | conflicting |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Benin 2018-19 | 35,042 | 42,343 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 35,042 | **0** | **0** |
| Burkina Faso 2018-19 | 45,612 | 45,612 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 45,612 | **0** | **0** |
| CotedIvoire 2018-19 | 61,116 | 61,116 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 61,116 | **0** | **0** |
| Guinea-Bissau 2018-19 | 42,839 | 42,839 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 42,839 | **0** | **0** |
| Senegal 2018-19 | 66,120 | 66,119 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 66,120 | **0** | **0** |
| Togo 2018 | 25,282 | 27,480 | 0 / 0 | 0 | 25,282 | **0** | **0** |

`groups == rows` on every line. No conflicting group exists to quote evidence for, because no duplicate group of any kind exists.

### Why the key cannot merge two people

1. `s04` is already one row per person (0 duplicate person-key groups).
2. `s01` likewise, so the `how='left'` roster merge fans out **0** rows in all six (`merged == len(s04)` exactly).
3. Every household-id formatter is **injective over the full roster**: 8,012 / 7,010 / 12,992 / 5,351 / 7,156 / 6,171 distinct `(grappe, menage)` pairs → the same number of distinct `i`. Zero collisions.

The two that could plausibly have collided, checked explicitly:

- **Burkina Faso**: `menage` runs to **527** — the three-digit case that broke the older `i()` (the GAP-4 livestock i-key bug). `ehcvm_i`'s `'0'` separator survives it cleanly.
- **CotedIvoire**: concatenates with **no separator**. Injective only because `menage` tops out at 30, so `zeropadding=3` always yields exactly three characters. **A future CotedIvoire wave with `menage > 999` would break this** — flagged in the comment at that site. This is the one latent key risk the review found, and it is prospective, not present.

Cold rebuilds confirm end to end: wave parquets carry exactly the pre-groupby row counts (Togo 25,282; Benin 35,042; Senegal 66,120), zero duplicate index entries.

### Left alone, on purpose

`.first()` unchanged (`skipna=False` withdrawn as a regression — each site comment now says why, so it is not re-derived), no `aggregation:` key (D1), nothing under `lsms_library/*.py`.

### Three side observations from the sweep

- **`dropna=False` is inert at all six sites.** Rows with NA `i`/`pid` are filtered on the line immediately above and `t` is a literal. Consistent with your reading that the kwarg is widely misunderstood; here it is merely redundant.
- **Senegal has one orphan person** — `(grappe 481, menage 9, line 17)` is in `s04` but not `s01`, so `Age`/`working_age` is NA for them. Roster gap, not a key defect.
- **Senegal's API row count is 65,723 vs. the parquet's 66,120.** I chased this because a silent 397-row loss is exactly what a broken key looks like. It is neither: all 7,156 wave households are in `sample()` at `t='2018-19'` with zero NA `v`, `_join_v_from_sample` drops nothing, `id_walk` drops nothing (`updated_ids['2018-19']` is empty). It is the universal hollow-row net `df.dropna(how='all')` at `country.py:2243`, removing 397 persons whose every declared column is NA (unknown age *and* non-1/2 codes on all three dummies). Benin and Togo have 0 such rows. Working as designed.

### What this leaves open on #637

Six of the 38 country-script sites are now genuinely measured. The remaining 32 — Tanzania's 16, Malawi's, Niger's `niger.py:1064` (the same EHCVM line, a seventh instance not in my scope), Uganda's two, `EthiopiaRHS` — are still unexercised for the reason you identified: the probe needs to reach the subprocess. Worth noting that for this cluster the direct source measurement was *cheaper* than plumbing a `sitecustomize.py` hook, and gives a stronger answer (it proves the key is sound, not merely that today's build happened not to fabricate).

PR: #638

## Key-soundness review: the six sites outside the EHCVM cluster

Taking the corrected reading — this issue is *"an inventory of sites whose correctness depends on their key being sound"* — I reviewed the six non-EHCVM, non-Tanzania, non-Malawi sites. **PR #646.**

Method: patch `DataFrameGroupBy.first` **in-process** and run each wave/country script directly (`runpy`), which sidesteps the `materialize: make` subprocess blind spot noted above — all six sites were actually observed. Cold builds, `LSMS_NO_CACHE=1` + isolated `LSMS_DATA_DIR`. Every duplicate group classified exact / complementary / conflicting.

| site | dup groups | exact | compl. | conflicting | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `Burkina_Faso/2014/_/food_coping.py:83` | **0** | 0 | 0 | 0 | **sound** |
| `Burkina_Faso/2014/_/months_food_inadequate.py:58` | **0** | 0 | 0 | 0 | **sound** |
| `EthiopiaRHS/_/ethiopiarhs.py:443` | **0** | 0 | 0 | 0 | **sound** |
| `Uganda/_/uganda.py:1470` (`plot_inputs`) | 1,342 | 1,300 | 0 | 42 | **BROKEN — fixed in #646** |
| `Niger/_/niger.py:1064` (`people_last7days`) | 210 | 34 | 6 | 170 | **BROKEN — wider than the site** |
| `Uganda/_/uganda.py:1088` (`crop_production`) | 3,654 | 2,709 | 112 | 833 | **BROKEN — wider than the site** |

### The `exact` column is not reassurance

For both broken Uganda keys, "exact" means only that the *payload columns* agreed. The rows still came from **different entities** and their `Quantity` was still summed. `crop_production` 2009-10 and 2010-11 have **no month column at all**, so 100% of their groups classify "exact" while fresh and dry harvest weights are added together.

**So conflict counts are a lower bound on the entity merge, not a measure of it.** Worth recording for the rest of the inventory: a site can be 100%-exact and still be silently merging two real things.

### 1. Uganda `plot_inputs` — fixed

`AGSEC3A` / `AGSEC3B` are two distinct plot-**season** questionnaires; the same plot id appears in both; the key had no `season`. ~95% of collisions were season-A/season-B pairs. 6 groups per wave reported the same pesticide in **different units**:

```
HH 1063000910, plot 1063000910-1-1, Insecticide
  season A: 70.0 Litre      season B: 1.0 Kg
  old key -> ONE row, Quantity 71.0, u 'Litre'
```

The repo had **already decided this key** — the sibling `plot_labor` builder reads the same two files and carries `season` because *"collapsing the two seasons into one (plot, source) row would require summing across seasons (a transformation)"*. `crop_production` carries it too; `plot_inputs` was the outlier. Fix is to the identifier (D1): **83,019 → 84,216 rows, +1,197 recovered**, index now unique in every wave so the collapse never fires, Quantity totals unchanged.

### 2. Niger `people_last7days` — 2014-15 only, needs a wave-wide `i` change

2011-12 / 2018-19 / 2021-22 are clean (25,125 / 35,406 / 44,320 rows, zero duplicates).

ECVMA2 keys households on `(GRAPPE, MENAGE, EXTENSION)`; `niger.i` drops `EXTENSION`. **3,617 distinct households collapse to 3,558** — 59 have no id of their own, and their members' line numbers collide. 420 rows in 210 groups, **`EXTENSION` differs in 210 of 210 (100%)**. Different real people:

```
GRAPPE 2, MENAGE 1, line 1 -> EXTENSION 0: age 56, industry 316
                              EXTENSION 2: age 29, industry 321
GRAPPE 2, MENAGE 1, line 2 -> EXTENSION 0: age 11
                              EXTENSION 2: age 22
```

This is precisely *"two people collapsed onto one `pid`"*.

**Not fixed in #646**: dropping `EXTENSION` is a wave-wide convention — `sample`, `household_roster` (same source file, same 210 collisions), `individual_education`, `livestock`, `crop_production`, `plot_inputs`, `plot_labor` all key on `(GRAPPE, MENAGE)`. Re-keying one table would break its join to `sample()` and the `panel_ids` chain. Needs `EXTENSION` added to `i` across the 2014-15 wave plus a `panel_ids` re-derivation.

### 3. Uganda `crop_production` — needs a grain decision

`AGSEC5A`/`5B` record **multiple distinct harvest records** per plot-crop-season; the key has no level for which record a row is.

**2009-16** — split by harvest **condition** (`a5aq6b`), season A: condition differs in **222/257, 277/328, 339/363, 223/254, 370/397** colliding groups (84–93%). Adding it drops 2011-12 from 363 groups to 24.

```
2011-12  HH 1033000506  plot -1-6  Coffee  Kilogram (KG)
  240 kg "Dry after additional drying - in pods or shell/husks"
  100 kg "Fresh/raw harvested - in pods or shell/husks"
  -> summed to 340 kg    (dry weight added to fresh weight)
```

**2019-20** — split by **instance** (`_1`/`_2` column groups: quantity, unit *and* month of a first and second harvest). 1,382 of 8,429 rows report both; 369 share a unit and collide.

**Not fixed in #646**: the missing level means two different things in two questionnaire vintages (a condition *vocabulary* vs an instance *ordinal*), so naming it is a grain decision for a published table rather than a bug fix. Per D1 the answer must be a new index level, never a reducer. Measurements are recorded at the site; happy to take a steer on the level's name and vocabulary and do it as its own PR.

### Notes for the rest of the inventory

- The in-process `runpy` harness works on `materialize: make` tables and needs no `sitecustomize.py`; reusable for the remaining sites.
- Three of six keys were sound and their `.first()` calls are pure dead code — the static-risk framing holds, but the "review the key" verdict is cheap to reach and worth doing per site rather than assuming.

## Tanzania (21 sites) — reviewed. **One key is broken: 2008-15 `shocks` is keyed on the panel LINE, not the household.**

Closing out the largest remaining block in the inventory. **PR #651.** Method as in #646: patch `DataFrameGroupBy.first` in-process and run each script via `runpy`, which sidesteps the `materialize: make` subprocess blind spot — so all 21 sites were actually observed. Cold builds, isolated `LSMS_DATA_DIR` with `dvc-cache` symlinked, `LSMS_COUNTRIES_ROOT` asserted at the worktree, no `dvc` CLI. `cluster_features` left alone (PR #642 owns it).

The issue's prose says "Tanzania — 16 sites"; the inventory table below it lists **21** Tanzania rows. All 21 are covered here.

| site | key | dup groups | exact | compl. | conflicting | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `2008-15/_/anthropometry.py:70` | `(t,i,pid)` | **0** | – | – | – | sound |
| `2008-15/_/food_coping.py:76` | `(t,i,Strategy)` | 54,495 | 54,495 | 0 | 0 | **sound** — de-replication |
| `2008-15/_/household_roster.py:37` | `(t,i,pid)` | **0** | – | – | – | sound |
| `2008-15/_/housing.py:43` | `(t,i)` | 8,488 | 8,488 | 0 | 0 | **sound** — de-replication |
| `2008-15/_/individual_education.py:52` | `(t,i,pid)` | **0** | – | – | – | sound |
| `2008-15/_/life_satisfaction.py:106` | `(t,i,Domain)` | **0** | – | – | – | sound |
| `2008-15/_/shocks.py:68` | `(t,i,Shock)`, **i = UPHI** | **0** | – | – | – | **BROKEN — fixed in #651** |
| `2019-20/_/*.py` (5 sites) | – | **0** each | – | – | – | sound |
| `2020-21/_/*.py` (5 sites) | – | **0** each | – | – | – | sound |
| `_/anthropometry.py:59` | `(t,i,pid)` | **0** | – | – | – | sound |
| `_/individual_education.py:59` | `(t,i,pid)` | **0** | – | – | – | sound |
| `_/tanzania.py:1686` (`people_last7days`) | `(t,i,pid)` | **0** both waves | – | – | – | sound |
| `_/tanzania.py:1822` (`community_prices`) | `(t,v,j,u)` | 261 / 1,281 | 18 / 132 | 0 | 243 / 1,149 | grain deliberate; arbitrary resolution **flagged, not fixed** |

### The broken key was invisible to a duplicate count

This is worth recording as a **third trap**, alongside the two already on this issue.

`2008-15/_/shocks.py` had **zero** duplicate groups. Its `.first()` was dead code. By every measure this issue's probe collects, the site was clean — and yet its key was the one broken key in the country, because `i` was built from **`UPHI`**, the NPS panel-tracking *line* index (`"1".."14985"`), not from `r_hhid`, the household id `sample`, `household_roster` and `updated_ids.json` all use.

The two namespaces shared **zero** values. Per wave, overlap of `shocks().i` with `household_roster().i`:

| wave | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2008-09 | **0** of 5,587 | 2,951 of 2,951 |
| 2010-11 | **0** of 6,875 | 3,285 of 3,285 |
| 2012-13 | **0** of 7,745 | 3,842 of 3,842 |
| 2014-15 | **0** of 3,634 | 3,166 of 3,166 |
| 2019-20 | 502 of 502 | unchanged |
| 2020-21 | 2,552 of 2,552 | unchanged |

Note the shape of the failure: the two later waves key on `sdd_hhid` / `y5_hhid` and always overlapped by 100%, so an aggregate check across the country would have looked fine. Only the per-wave split shows it.

**Duplicates were absent precisely BECAUSE the key was broken.** The upd4 household-level modules record a household-round once per *descendant panel line* — the replication `sample.py:54` documents for the cover page (29,250 rows → 16,540 household-rounds, group sizes 1..11). Keyed on the line, each copy became its own "household", so nothing collided:

```
round 1, r_hhid 01010140020171 — 3 shocks, recorded on UPHI lines 1, 2, 3
  UPHI 1  CROP DISEASE OR CROP PESTS    INCOME LOSS
  UPHI 2  CROP DISEASE OR CROP PESTS    INCOME LOSS
  UPHI 3  CROP DISEASE OR CROP PESTS    INCOME LOSS
  ... x3 for each of the other two shocks
  old key -> households "1", "2", "3"; 9 rows; each shock counted 3x
```

74,341 wave rows stood for 39,724 household-shock facts — any count of who suffered a shock inflated ~1.9×. `id_walk` also matched nothing, so the four rounds never formed a panel.

Fix is the identifier (D1): `i = r_hhid`. That re-exposes the replication as duplicates, which the existing `.first()` collapses — **de-replication, not a choice**: over the whole module (449,435 rows, 134,035 duplicate `(round, r_hhid, hr_00)` groups) **zero** groups differ on any of the nine `hr_*` columns. The script now asserts that before collapsing, per `sample.py:76`'s discipline. API: 60,463 → 35,746 rows, 0 `(t, i)` pairs unknown to `sample()`, 0 `id_walk` collisions.

Historical note: **GH #132** filed this table's 60% duplicate `(t, i, Shock)` rate. Keying on UPHI removed the duplicates without fixing the entity — the symptom went away and the identifier got worse. Exactly what D1 exists to prevent.

### "exact" again, and how it was actually settled

`housing` and `food_coping` are 100% "exact" (8,488 and 54,495 duplicate groups, **0** conflicting). Per your trap-1 note I did not treat that as the evidence. What settles them:

- **No source column at all differs** within a duplicate group — housing: 0 of 8,488 groups differ on any of the **74** `hi_*` columns, including continuous ones like `hi_04` (rent), and including the 59 round-4 groups `sample.py` flags as cluster-ambiguous; food_coping: 0 of 6,814 differ on any `hh_*` column, not merely the 8 items read.
- **Lineage**, independently: a round-1 household with *k* panel lines maps to *k* **distinct** round-4 households in 174 of the 211 cases where more than one of its lines is still observed in round 4. That is the positive form of "these are copies of one household", rather than the absence of a conflict.
- The two modules' per-round duplicate counts (R2 2,698 / R3 3,628 / R4 488) are **identical** — the same replication seen through two modules.

Trap 2 (invariance by missingness) does not bite here: every column tested is densely populated (0 null `UPI` over 83,706 rows; 0 null `sdd_hhid`/`y5_hhid`; `hr_01` present on all 449,435 shock rows).

### The 15 dead-code sites — checked on the key, not the count

`.first()` never fires. Rather than record that and stop:

- The 2008-15 **individual**-level modules (`_b`, `_v`, `_c`, `_g`) carry `(r_hhid, UPI)` and **no `UPHI` column**, which is *why* the replication does not reach them: 83,706 rows / 83,706 groups / 0 duplicates each; pid formatting injective (45,396 → 45,396).
- Head reductions checked directly, since they are what make `(t, i, Domain)` a key: exactly one `HEAD` per household-round — 16,540/16,540, 1,183/1,183, 4,709/4,709.
- 2019-20 / 2020-21 sources `(hhid, indid)`-unique, `format_id` injective (1,184 → 1,184; 4,709 → 4,709), shocks `(hhid, shock_id)`-unique after the YES filter.
- Country-level concatenators: disjoint `t` per folder, `id_walk` renames only `i`, 0 collisions measured.

### Flagged, not fixed: `community_prices` (`_/tanzania.py:1822`)

`(t, v, j, u)` **is** the declared grain and the collisions are exactly the intended `harmonize_community_price` label lump — checked, not assumed: of 261 colliding groups in 2019-20 and 1,281 in 2020-21, **261 / 1,281 span more than one source item code and ZERO repeat a code**. So the survey never prices the same item twice in a cluster, and no additional level exists that would not break the shared `j` this feature exists to join on.

What the collapse *does* do is resolve genuine disagreement arbitrarily — 243 / 1,149 groups hold more than one distinct observed price:

```
2020-21  cluster 01-06-47-85  "Millet & Sorghum (grain)"  per Kg
    item 6:   2,000 TSh     item 7:  16,000 TSh
    -> .first() keeps 2,000
```

That is the #323 Option-B discussion you separated out, not this issue, and per D1 the answer may not be a reducer. Recorded at the site with its measurements. Also corrected there, **doc only**: the comment said the collision was combined "by their MEAN"; the code has always taken the first — two contradictory paragraphs one line apart.

### Test

`tests/test_gh637_tanzania_shocks_household_id.py`, 11 tests, asserting the *identifier* and row counts and **never** post-collapse index uniqueness — uniqueness held perfectly with the bug present, which is how it hid. **Negative control against a pristine `origin/development` config tree: all 11 fail.**

### What this leaves open on #637

With #638 (EHCVM six), #646 (six more) and #651 (Tanzania's 21), the remaining unmeasured country-script sites are **Malawi's** (3 multi-column + 7 dict-agg) and the two `Uganda/_/uganda.py` items #646 deferred (`crop_production`'s missing grain level, and Niger 2014-15's wave-wide `EXTENSION` re-key).

One suggestion for whoever takes Malawi: **the probe's duplicate count is not sufficient to clear a site.** Tanzania's one broken key produced zero duplicates. The question the inventory is really asking is "does `i` identify a household?", and the cheapest way to answer it is to intersect the built table's `i` with `sample()`'s, **per wave**.

## A third trap, and it inverts the instrument: **a broken key can produce ZERO duplicates**

From the Tanzania review (PR #651). Every method used on this issue so far hunts for *collisions* — duplicate groups, conflicting values. This defect produces the **opposite** signal, and would pass every check we have built.

`Tanzania/2008-15/_/shocks.py` built `i` from **`UPHI`** — the NPS panel-*line* index (`"1".."14985"`) — instead of `r_hhid`. The two namespaces share **zero** values.

Duplicates were absent **because** the key was broken: the upd4 modules replicate a household-round once per descendant line, so each replicated copy became its own distinct "household". Result: **74,341 rows carrying 39,724 facts**, shock counts inflated ~1.9x, and `id_walk` matching nothing at all.

Its `groupby().first()` therefore reported `0` duplicate groups — the same reading as a perfectly sound key.

### The check that would have caught it, and the one that would not

Per-wave overlap between the tables `i` values and `household_roster`s:

| wave | overlap |
|---|---|
| 2008-15 rounds | **0 of 5,587 / 6,875 / 7,745 / 3,634** |
| 2019-20 | 100% |
| 2020-21 | 100% |

**An aggregate overlap check would have passed** — the two clean waves mask the four broken ones. Only the per-wave view shows it.

### Consequence for how the rest of this inventory gets cleared

Add to the two traps already recorded (`"exact" is not reassurance`; `invariance by missingness`):

> **3. Zero duplicates is not evidence of a sound key.** A key drawn from the wrong namespace fragments rather than collides. Verify that the tables `i` values actually LIVE in the household universe — per wave, never in aggregate — rather than concluding from the absence of collisions.

Cheap concrete test: `set(df.index.get_level_values("i")) & set(roster_i)` per wave, and separately compare row count against the count of distinct underlying facts. Tanzanias fix took the API from **60,463 to 35,746 rows** — a 41% reduction that no duplicate-count instrument could have predicted.

Fixed at the identifier per D1 (`i = r_hhid`), with the re-exposed replication collapsed by the existing `.first()` under a new assert (0 of 134,035 groups differ on any `hr_*` column). Negative control: all 11 new tests fail against pristine `origin/development`.
